title: Durable Candidate Preparation Jobs
summary: P3A explicitly queues, prepares and verifies an isolated candidate without changing the active publication. PostgreSQL owns job state, worker leases, idempotency and audit; Core owns generation and verification.

configuration.limits: Unreleased jobs 1..64, lease 3..300 seconds. Configured max-retained-jobs times max-generation-bytes cannot exceed 1 GiB. Admission sums original reservations only for jobs not explicitly released by retention, so configuration changes cannot forget commitments. Historical job metadata has a separate 65536-row cap.
configuration.privacy: state_dir is canonical, nonsymlink, owned by the service user and inaccessible to group/other; it must not overlap configured project roots. Routes, profile bytes, root identity, state directory identity, candidate version and generation limits form the execution fingerprint.
configuration.migration: Migration 004 adds the enqueue-time expected_route_revision and active-generation tables. It was explicitly applied to the private test stand and retains its original checksum. Migration 005 adds the nullable paired audit_events activation_route_id and activation_previous_revision foreign key to the activation receipt. expected_snapshot_id remains the external preparation request precondition; enqueue captures the matching DB route revision internally. The original preparation milestone used config v4; author current configuration from docs/machine/shin-companion-protocols-v1.json and its check-config gate, not that historical version. The schema field here is a tested projection of that inventory. Preserve credentials, deployment identity and the PostgreSQL volume during an explicit reviewed configuration transition.

scope: Local authenticated development server, opt-in preparation worker, one worker per process and a private artifact namespace. P3D2 may select a freshly verified prepared artifact through the separate DB-only activation authority; this is not a distributed job platform.

api.POST /api/v1/projects/{project}/routes/{: Administrator and enabled worker required. Exact body {expected_snapshot_id: full fnv1a64 id or null}; Idempotency-Key required. Return 202 with job/replayed=false, or 200 replaying the same durable job. Acceptance is not verification success.
api.GET /api/v1/preparations: Read-only authorized keyset page, after and limit 1..100. Scope is applied before pagination.
api.GET /api/v1/preparations/{id}: Read-only public job record. Denied and missing jobs return 404. No worker token, input transcript, credential or local artifact path.
api.POST /api/v1/preparations/{id}/cancel: Administrator, exact empty JSON body. Queued jobs become cancelled; running jobs record cancel_requested. Repeated or terminal cancellation does not create another transition. A prepared artifact is not deleted or activated by cancellation.
api.GET /api/v1/preparation-worker: Administrator-only in-process enabled/state/last-error/active-job observation. It is not DB, source or artifact readiness.
api.noImplicitActions: Retrieval, health and GETs never enqueue, expire, cancel, repair or activate jobs. Only the explicitly enabled worker claims/reconciles queued work. Observer/watch attachment is not implemented.
api.candidateInspection: P3B adds a separate read-only GET /api/v1/preparations/{id}/inspection. The ordinary job GET remains historical metadata; see shin-server-candidate-inspection-v1.
api.activation: P3D2 uses GET/POST /api/v1/projects/{project}/routes/{route}/activation; POST has exact body {preparation_id: ID|null, expected_revision: integer}. Activation is a separately verified administrator action; see shin-server-activation-v1.

jobSemantics.sourceTiming: A job reads sources at execution time, not enqueue time. expected_snapshot_id is the unchanged external precondition on the active snapshot, not a source fingerprint or a request to freeze the worktree. Enqueue also captures the current DB route revision internally, so later activation cannot publish over a changed base.
jobSemantics.preparedMeaning: A separate artifact passed generated-integrity loading, strict Doctor and exact-current assessment during preparation. The timestamp is historical completion evidence, not a reusable current=true claim. GET does not revalidate retained artifact bytes or source freshness.
jobSemantics.activation: Preparation never activates itself. P3D2 activation re-runs strict profile-check, Doctor, exact-current, Eval and nonempty Pack-eval while candidate and Core publication shared locks are held, then commits the active DB reference, receipt and audit atomically. A callback is therefore inside the verification lifetime, not a reusable GET preflight token.
jobSemantics.safetyGates: Reject capped/skipped source-fact scans, oversized artifacts, strict Doctor errors or warnings, source drift, changed route/root/profile, mismatched base or lost lease. Core health is invoked through its typed API, never by capturing global stdout.
jobSemantics.identity: Snapshot identities retain their full fnv1a64: prefix. They detect drift and identify content, not cryptographic source authority. Route fingerprints use SHA256 over reviewed configuration.

ownership.claim: Transactional FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED selects a queued job once. A random per-process worker id and an unexpired PostgreSQL-clock lease fence renewals and completion.
ownership.renewal: A separate bounded heartbeat renews approximately every lease/3 while Core runs. Renewal fails on cancellation, expiry, wrong owner or database loss. The worker rechecks authority at phase boundaries and completion uses a guarded database update.
ownership.recovery: Queued jobs survive restart. Expired running jobs become failed/lease-expired, or cancelled if requested. Claimed jobs are never automatically requeued. A caller retries intentionally with a new idempotency key.
ownership.cancellation: Cooperative at phase boundaries; existing Core parsing and filesystem waits are not forcibly interrupted. Socket timeouts and leases are not hard execution deadlines. A process supervisor may terminate a stuck worker; durable state then recovers through lease expiry.
ownership.configurationChanges: A queued job whose principal or execution fingerprint no longer matches current configuration fails closed. It is not silently rebound to new paths, profiles or limits.
ownership.audit: Job transitions and management audit commit together; events include preparation_id. All audit writers retain the common commit-order lock before allocating event ids. Heartbeats do not generate unbounded audit events.

artifacts.layout: Private state_dir/job-<database id>-<artifact_key>; a unique random key and stable namespace binding are persisted by migration 003. Directory allocation is exclusive; the job is claimed once and its output remains separate from active routes.
artifacts.persistence: Synchronize generated data and parent directories before acknowledging prepared in PostgreSQL. Filesystem preparation and the database transition are separate operations; an uncertain DB acknowledgement never triggers artifact deletion.
artifacts.retention: P3C adds explicit plan/apply retention with durable intent and recovery; see shin-server-retention-v1. Failed, cancelled, interrupted and uncertain artifacts retain their reservation until deletion is confirmed and released is committed. No automatic cleanup. Historical job/idempotency records and lock inodes remain; old unbound artifacts fail closed.
artifacts.accounting: The reservation bounds generated payload, not filesystem metadata, transient generation memory, allocator overhead or total RSS. Source generation is profile-bounded and one worker runs per process; full hard memory/CPU isolation and power-loss recovery remain unverified.

sources.use: SKIP LOCKED for queue claim, not a consistent general retrieval view; row locking needs UPDATE permission.
Transaction-scoped locks and bounded lock ordering for claims, admission and audit.
